hypothesis: Under the linear-ICA hypothesis class (Z with independent non-Gaussian marginals, X = A*Z with A square orthogonal), sklearn FastICA achieves Amari index <= 0.02 at N = 10000 for every d_Z in {2, 4, 6, 8}; the smallest N reaching Amari <= 0.03 grows only polynomially in d_Z with fitted log-log slope b << 3.0; the Amari(N) curve at each d_Z is nonincreasing modulo a 0.01 numerical wobble; and the linear-ICA sample complexity at d_Z = 8 is at least 20x below the Theorem 6 exponential bound (D_Z=1, eps=0.25, eps_rel=0.05, c=1), witnessing SIC-C-c's partial positive resolution for the linear-ICA inductive-bias class.

controls.description: All randomness is derived from BASE_SEED = 0 via numpy SeedSequence keyed by (BASE_SEED, d_Z, trial), and sklearn FastICA random_state is set to the trial index; running twice yields identical Amari values at every grid point.

Within each trial, one (A, Z_full) is drawn at max(N_VALUES) and every smaller N re-uses the first N samples as a prefix, so the sample-complexity curve varies only in N and not in the underlying random stream.

Amari is averaged over TRIALS = 8 independent (A, Z) draws per grid point; finite-sample FastICA variance is smoothed enough that monotonicity holds within a 0.01 tolerance and the sample-complexity fit is stable.

The Amari index is verified to be exactly 0 on the identity matrix and on any signed permutation matrix (the ICA identifiability class), and > 0 on non-degenerate mixtures --- covered by the unit tests.

gates.criterion: Averaged Amari at N = 10000 is <= 0.02 for every d_Z in {2, 4, 6, 8}.
The smallest N in the sweep reaching averaged Amari <= 0.03 exists for every d_Z, and the linear regression log(N_needed) = a + b * log(d_Z) has fitted slope b <= 3.0.
For every d_Z, the averaged Amari curve is nonincreasing in N modulo a numerical tolerance of 0.01.
At d_Z = 8, the linear-ICA sample complexity to reach Amari <= 0.03 is at least 20x below the Theorem 6 bound ceil(1 * (1/0.25)^{8} * ln((1/0.25)^{8} / 0.05)) = 923146.
